scripts.passability_check_main

ROS node for defining a traversable corridor and monitoring its clearance.

The node activates after the door detector reports an opening. It projects aligned depth into the robot frame, defines either a frame-anchored or virtual corridor, updates that corridor from odometry, and publishes clearance and heading information to the traversal controller.

   1#!/usr/bin/env python3
   2"""ROS node for defining a traversable corridor and monitoring its clearance.
   3
   4The node activates after the door detector reports an opening. It projects
   5aligned depth into the robot frame, defines either a frame-anchored or virtual
   6corridor, updates that corridor from odometry, and publishes clearance and
   7heading information to the traversal controller.
   8"""

  28class PassabilityCheckerNode:
  29    """
  30    Define traversable corridors and monitor their obstacle clearance.
  31
  32    The node is activated by a door-opening result. It combines the detected
  33    door geometry, aligned RGB-D data, camera-to-robot extrinsics, and odometry
  34    to build a corridor in a fixed reference frame. As the robot moves, the
  35    stored corridor is propagated into the current robot frame before the next
  36    clearance measurement is published to the traversal controller.
  37
  38    The same processing loop can also perform short-range, robot-centric
  39    checks and can search the visible scene for a virtual corridor when the
  40    original door corridor is no longer usable.
  41
  42    Attributes:
  43        active:
  44            Whether image and odometry processing is enabled.
  45
  46        color_image:
  47            Latest BGR color frame, or ``None`` before one is received.
  48
  49        depth_image:
  50            Latest aligned depth image in meters.
  51
  52        fx:
  53            Camera focal length along the image x axis, in pixels.
  54
  55        R_rc:
  56            Rotation matrix that maps camera-frame vectors into the robot
  57            ``trunk`` frame.
  58
  59        t_rc:
  60            Camera origin expressed in the robot frame, in meters.
  61
  62        requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node:
  63            Requested mode: ``0`` disables checks, ``1`` checks the stored
  64            corridor, and ``2`` checks the space directly ahead.
  65
  66        corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis:
  67            Current signed distance to the corridor midpoint, measured along
  68            the corridor axis in meters.
  69
  70        passability_checker:
  71            Point-cloud filtering pipeline used to find the nearest obstacle.
  72    """
  73

 274    def get_camera_extrinsics_tf(self,
 275                                robot_frame="trunk",
 276                                camera_frame="realsense_d455_optical_frame"
 277                                ):
 278        """
 279        Read the camera pose in the robot frame from TF.
 280
 281        The returned transform maps an optical-frame point ``p_c`` to the
 282        robot frame as ``p_r = R_rc @ p_c + t_rc``. The camera optical axes are
 283        right, down, and forward; the robot axes are forward, left, and up.
 284
 285        Args:
 286            robot_frame:
 287                Target robot frame in which points should be expressed.
 288
 289            camera_frame:
 290                Source optical frame attached to the depth camera.
 291
 292        Returns:
 293            A tuple ``(R_rc, t_rc)`` containing a ``3 x 3`` rotation matrix and
 294            a three-element translation vector in meters.
 295
 296        Raises:
 297            tf2_ros.LookupException:
 298                If no transform is available for the named frames.
 299
 300            tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
 301                If the TF tree cannot connect the frames.
 302
 303            tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
 304                If TF cannot satisfy the requested timestamp.
 305
 306        Notes:
 307            This method is intended to run once after the robot and camera
 308            frames have been published. It waits up to five seconds in the
 309            initial availability check.
 310
 311        """
 312
 313
 314        tf_buffer = tf2_ros.Buffer()
 315        tf_listener = tf2_ros.TransformListener(tf_buffer)
 316
 317        rospy.loginfo("Waiting for TF %s -> %s",
 318                    robot_frame, camera_frame)
 319
 320        # Wait until TF is available
 321        tf_buffer.can_transform(
 322            robot_frame,
 323            camera_frame,
 324            rospy.Time(0),
 325            rospy.Duration(5.0)
 326        )
 327
 328        transform = tf_buffer.lookup_transform(
 329            robot_frame,
 330            camera_frame,
 331            rospy.Time(0)
 332        )
 333
 334        # Translation
 335        t = transform.transform.translation
 336        t_rc = np.array([t.x, t.y, t.z])
 337
 338        # Rotation (quaternion → matrix)
 339        q = transform.transform.rotation
 340        quat = [q.x, q.y, q.z, q.w]
 341        R_rc = R.from_quat(quat).as_matrix()
 342
 343        rospy.loginfo("Camera extrinsics loaded from TF")
 344        print("R_rc =\n", R_rc)
 345        test = np.array([0, 0, 1])  # camera forward
 346        print("Camera forward in robot frame:", R_rc @ test)
 347
 348
 349
 350        return R_rc, t_rc
 351

 353    def _activate_node_cb(self, msg):
 354        """
 355        Activate passability processing for an eligible door state.
 356
 357        Args:
 358            msg:
 359                ROS ``String`` containing the detected door state.
 360
 361        Notes:
 362            ``open_left``, ``open_right``, ``No_door_plane_detected``, and
 363            ``no_frame_detected`` start a new cycle. The first accepted state is
 364            retained as the basis for corridor definition.
 365        """
 366        if msg.data in ["open_left", "open_right", "No_door_plane_detected", "no_frame_detected"]: # one time activation on these states
 367            if not self.active:
 368                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: activated")
 369                self.active = True
 370                #to create subscriptions
 371                self.activate_camera()
 372                self.get_odom()
 373                # store the door open status only once at activation
 374                self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data 
 375                self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection = True  # to define new corridor on next run
 376                
 377            
 378
 379    def _deactivate_node_cb(self, msg):
 380        """
 381        End the active passability cycle after traversal completes.
 382
 383        Args:
 384            msg:
 385                ROS ``Bool`` message. Only a true value causes deactivation.
 386
 387        Notes:
 388            The callback unregisters conditional subscribers, clears
 389            cycle-specific geometry, and asks the door detector to start its
 390            next detection cycle.
 391        """
 392        if msg.data:  # only deactivate on True
 393            if self.active:
 394                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: deactivated by traversal done signal")
 395                self.deactivate_camera()
 396                self.deactivate_odom()
 397            self.active = False
 398            self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection = False
 399            self.trigger_traversal_node = False # to deactivate traversal node. because door is already traversed
 400            # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 401            self.x_corridor_center_cam_first_time = None
 402            self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node = None
 403            self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node = 1 # reset to default 1 for corridor
 404            self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node = None
 405            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node = None
 406            self.plane_info_distance_m = None
 407            self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame = None
 408            self.virtual_corridor_definition_finished = False
 409            self.corridor_middle_point_depth_from_traversal = None
 410            self.retrigger_door_detection_node_pub.publish(True) # to retrigger door detection node for next detection and traversal cycle
 411

 418    def activate_camera(self):
 419        """
 420        Subscribe to the color, aligned-depth, and camera-info topics.
 421
 422        Notes:
 423            Each subscriber is created only if it is not already active, so
 424            repeated activation requests are safe.
 425        """
 426        if self.color_sub is None:
 427            self.color_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 428                self.color_topic,
 429                Image,
 430                self._color_cb,
 431                queue_size=1
 432            )
 433        if self.depth_sub is None:
 434            self.depth_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 435                self.depth_topic,
 436                Image,
 437                self._depth_cb,
 438                queue_size=1
 439            )
 440        if self.info_sub is None:
 441            self.info_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 442                self.camera_info_topic,
 443                CameraInfo,
 444                self._info_cb,
 445                queue_size=1
 446            )
 447    
 448    def deactivate_camera(self):
 449        """
 450        Unregister camera subscribers and discard their cached data.
 451
 452        Notes:
 453            Clearing the cached frames forces a later activation cycle to wait
 454            for fresh camera data instead of reusing an old observation.
 455        """
 456        for sub in [self.color_sub, self.depth_sub, self.info_sub]:
 457            if sub is not None:
 458                sub.unregister()
 459
 460        self.color_sub = None
 461        self.depth_sub = None
 462        self.info_sub = None
 463
 464
 465        # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 466        self.color_image = None
 467        self.depth_image = None
 468        self.latest_info = None
 469    
 470        
 471
 472    def get_odom(self):
 473        """
 474        Subscribe to robot odometry when it is not already active.
 475
 476        Notes:
 477            The first odometry sample received after subscription establishes
 478            the node-activation reference pose.
 479        """
 480        if self.odom_sub is None:
 481            self.odom_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 482                "/odom_bridge_output",
 483                Odometry,
 484                self._odom_callback,
 485                queue_size=1
 486            )
 487
 488    def deactivate_odom(self):
 489        """
 490        Unregister odometry and clear all cached planar poses.
 491
 492        Notes:
 493            Both the current pose and the activation reference are reset so
 494            that the next cycle starts in a new local reference frame.
 495        """
 496        if self.odom_sub is not None:
 497            self.odom_sub.unregister()
 498            self.odom_sub = None
 499        # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 500        self.start_pose_at_node_activation = None
 501        self.start_yaw_at_node_activation = None
 502        self.current_pose = None
 503        self.current_yaw = None
 504
 505    # -----------------------------
 506    # Callbacks (store only!)
 507    # -----------------------------
 508    def _color_cb(self, color_msg):
 509        """
 510        Convert and cache the latest ROS color image.
 511
 512        Args:
 513            color_msg:
 514                ROS ``Image`` converted to an OpenCV BGR image with
 515                ``CvBridge``.
 516
 517        Raises:
 518            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
 519                If the message cannot be converted as ``bgr8``.
 520        """
 521        self.color_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(color_msg, "bgr8")
 522
 523    def _depth_cb(self, depth_msg):
 524        """
 525        Convert and cache the latest depth image in meters.
 526
 527        Args:
 528            depth_msg:
 529                ROS ``Image`` containing millimeter ``16UC1``/``mono16`` depth
 530                or a floating-point depth representation.
 531
 532        Raises:
 533            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
 534                If the ROS image cannot be converted.
 535        """
 536        img = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(depth_msg, "passthrough")
 537
 538        if depth_msg.encoding in ("16UC1", "mono16"):
 539            depth_mm = img.astype(np.uint16)
 540            depth_m = depth_mm.astype(np.float32) / 1000.0
 541        else:
 542            depth_m = img.astype(np.float32)
 543
 544        self.depth_image = depth_m
 545
 546    def _info_cb(self, info_msg: CameraInfo):
 547        """
 548        Cache camera calibration from the first camera-info message.
 549
 550        Args:
 551            info_msg:
 552                ROS ``CameraInfo`` whose intrinsic matrix follows the standard
 553                row-major ``K`` layout.
 554
 555        Notes:
 556            Calibration is treated as constant during a run; later messages
 557            are ignored.
 558        """
 559        # storing the camera intrinsics only once. it will not change during runtime
 560        if self.latest_info is None:
 561            self.latest_info = info_msg
 562            K = info_msg.K
 563            self.fx, self.fy = K[0], K[4]
 564            self.cx, self.cy = K[2], K[5]
 565            rospy.loginfo("Camera intrinsics received and stored.")
 566    
 567    def _mid_frame_x_px_cb(self, msg):
 568        """
 569        Store the first valid door-frame midpoint pixel of an active cycle.
 570
 571        Args:
 572            msg:
 573                ROS ``Int32`` containing the horizontal image coordinate.
 574
 575        Notes:
 576            Non-positive values and samples received while inactive are
 577            ignored.
 578        """
 579        if msg.data <= 0: # invalid pixel
 580            return
 581        # only update if not set. which means take only first valid pixel after activation
 582        # checking self.active will make sure we get door depth and mid frame only when door state is open
 583        if self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node is None and self.active:
 584            self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data
 585
 586    def _plane_info_cb(self, msg):
 587        """
 588        Store the first valid detected door-plane measurement.
 589
 590        Args:
 591            msg:
 592                ROS ``Twist`` used as a compact container. ``linear.x`` is
 593                plane distance in meters, while ``angular.(x, y, z)`` contains
 594                the camera-frame normal.
 595
 596        Notes:
 597            A non-positive distance is invalid. Only the first valid sample in
 598            an active cycle is retained.
 599        """
 600        # plane info is published as Twist for simplicity, where:
 601        # linear.x = distance_m, angular.x = plane_norm_x, angular.y = plane_norm_y, angular.z = plane_norm_z
 602        if msg.linear.x <= 0.0: # invalid distance
 603            return
 604        if self.plane_info_distance_m is None and self.active:
 605            self.plane_info_distance_m = msg.linear.x
 606            self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame = np.array([msg.angular.x, msg.angular.y, msg.angular.z])
 607            rospy.loginfo(f"Received plane info from frame detection node: distance {self.plane_info_distance_m:.2f} m, normal vector {self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame}")
 608
 609    def _request_local_passability_check_cb(self, msg):
 610        """
 611        Store the passability mode requested by the traversal controller.
 612
 613        Args:
 614            msg:
 615                ROS ``UInt8``: ``0`` disables checking, ``1`` requests the
 616                corridor mode, and ``2`` requests the local mode.
 617        """
 618        if msg.data in [0, 1, 2]: # 1 for corridor , 2 for local
 619            self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node = msg.data
 620    
 621    def _request_new_corridor_definition_cb(self, msg):
 622        """
 623        Record a traversal-side request for a virtual corridor.
 624
 625        Args:
 626            msg:
 627                ROS ``Twist`` used as a request container. A truthy
 628                ``linear.x`` enables the request and ``linear.y`` supplies the
 629                desired corridor-midpoint depth in meters.
 630
 631        Notes:
 632            Requests are accepted only while the node is active.
 633        """
 634        if msg.linear.x:  # only activate on True
 635            if self.active:
 636                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: New corridor definition requested by traversal node")
 637                self.define_new_corridor_req_from_traversal = True  # to define new corridor on next run
 638                self.corridor_middle_point_depth_from_traversal = msg.linear.y  # to define new corridor based on this depth
 639

 642    def _door_depth_cb(self, msg):
 643        """
 644        Store the first valid detected door depth of an active cycle.
 645
 646        Args:
 647            msg:
 648                ROS ``Float32`` containing depth in meters.
 649
 650        Notes:
 651            Non-positive samples and later samples from the same cycle are
 652            ignored.
 653        """
 654        if msg.data <= 0.0: # invalid depth
 655            return
 656        # only update if not set. which means take only first valid depth after activation
 657        # checking self.active will make sure we get door depth and mid frame only when door state is open
 658        if self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node is None and self.active:
 659            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data

 661    def _odom_callback(self, msg):
 662        """
 663        Cache planar odometry and establish the activation reference pose.
 664
 665        Args:
 666            msg:
 667                ROS ``Odometry`` containing the robot position and quaternion
 668                orientation.
 669
 670        Notes:
 671            The first sample after activation is stored separately so later
 672            displacement can be measured relative to the start of the cycle.
 673        """
 674        p = msg.pose.pose.position
 675        q = msg.pose.pose.orientation
 676
 677
 678        self.current_pose = (p.x, p.y)
 679
 680        quat = [q.x, q.y, q.z, q.w]
 681        _, _, yaw = euler_from_quaternion(quat)
 682        self.current_yaw = yaw
 683        # store the start pose and yaw at activation.run only once
 684        if self.start_pose_at_node_activation is None:
 685            self.start_pose_at_node_activation = (p.x, p.y)
 686            self.start_yaw_at_node_activation = yaw
 687

 694    def first_time_data_ready_after_node_activation(self):
 695        """
 696        Check whether initial corridor-definition inputs are available.
 697
 698        Returns:
 699            ``True`` when color, depth, intrinsics, door state, door depth, and
 700            the activation pose have all been received; otherwise ``False``.
 701        """
 702        return (
 703            self.color_image is not None and
 704            self.depth_image is not None and
 705            self.fx is not None and
 706            self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node is not None and
 707            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node is not None and
 708            self.start_pose_at_node_activation is not None and
 709            self.start_yaw_at_node_activation is not None
 710        )
 711
 712    def get_forward_displacement_since_start(self):
 713        """
 714        Measure motion along the corridor-definition heading.
 715
 716        Returns:
 717            Signed displacement in meters along the yaw recorded when the
 718            current corridor was defined.
 719
 720        Notes:
 721            Projecting world translation onto a fixed heading keeps the result
 722            independent of later yaw corrections.
 723        """
 724
 725        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 726        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 727
 728        return dx * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 729    
 730    def get_lateral_displacement_since_start(self):
 731        """
 732        Measure motion perpendicular to the corridor-definition heading.
 733
 734        Returns:
 735            Signed lateral displacement in meters in the reference frame that
 736            was active when the corridor was defined.
 737
 738        Notes:
 739            The sign follows the left-handed lateral basis produced by
 740            ``(-sin(yaw), cos(yaw))``.
 741        """
 742
 743        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 744        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 745
 746        return -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 747    
 748    def calculate_dynamic_x_corridor_center_in_cameraframe(self):
 749        """
 750        Estimate the apparent lateral corridor shift from odometry.
 751
 752        Translation perpendicular to the initial heading and the image shift
 753        caused by accumulated yaw are added together.
 754
 755        Returns:
 756            Estimated horizontal corridor-center displacement in meters.
 757
 758        Notes:
 759            The rotational term uses the current distance to the corridor
 760            midpoint, so the estimate grows as heading error acts over a longer
 761            viewing distance.
 762        """
 763
 764        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 765        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 766        
 767        #translation effect
 768        # Project displacement onto perpendicular to initial heading
 769        lateral_displacement = -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 770
 771        #rotation effect
 772        # rotation effect
 773        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
 774        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
 775
 776        rotation_shift = (self.corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis * np.tan(delta_yaw))
 777    
 778        
 779        rospy.loginfo(f"start pose is {self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition} and current pose is {self.current_pose}   Lateral displacement from start: {lateral_displacement:.3f} m   Rotation shift: {rotation_shift:.3f} m")
 780        
 781        
 782        return (
 783        lateral_displacement
 784        + rotation_shift
 785    )
 786
 787    
 788
 789    def find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(self, final_points_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance):
 790        """
 791        Slide a robot-width window and choose a clear centerline.
 792
 793        Candidate centers span the camera field of view in corridor
 794        coordinates. A candidate is valid when its nearest obstacle is beyond
 795        ``min_clearance``. Among valid candidates, the center closest to the
 796        robot's current forward axis is preferred.
 797
 798        Args:
 799            final_points_robot_frame:
 800                ``N x 2`` array of filtered obstacle points on the robot-frame
 801                ground plane, in meters.
 802
 803            z_max:
 804                Far search distance in meters. It defines the visible lateral
 805                span and is used as clearance when a candidate contains no
 806                obstacle points.
 807
 808            min_clearance:
 809                Minimum acceptable forward clearance in meters.
 810
 811        Returns:
 812            Lateral center coordinate of the best corridor in meters, or
 813            ``None`` when no robot-width candidate meets the clearance
 814            requirement.
 815
 816        Notes:
 817            Candidate width includes the configured robot half-width and safety
 818            margin.
 819        """
 820        # find best corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
 821        # final points are in robot frame
 822
 823
 824        forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 825        lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 826
 827
 828        H, W = self.depth_image.shape
 829        x_edge_camera_frame = (W / 2.0) * z_max / self.fx
 830
 831        left_edge_camera_frame  = np.array([-x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
 832        right_edge_camera_frame = np.array([ x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
 833
 834        left_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ left_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
 835        right_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ right_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
 836
 837        left_edge_corridor_frame = left_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 838        right_edge_corridor_frame = right_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 839
 840        lat_min_corridor_frame = min(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
 841        lat_max_corridor_frame = max(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
 842        slide_centers_corridor_frame = np.arange(lat_min_corridor_frame + self.half_width, lat_max_corridor_frame - self.half_width, self.slide_step_x_direction)
 843        # because lateral min and max depends on entire image,not just on the obstacle points. 
 844
 845        valid_corridors = []
 846
 847        for lat_c in slide_centers_corridor_frame:
 848            x_left  = lat_c - self.half_width
 849            x_right = lat_c + self.half_width
 850
 851            corridor_mask = (
 852                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame > x_left) &
 853                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame < x_right)
 854            )
 855
 856            corridor_forward_coordinates = forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame[corridor_mask]
 857
 858            # no points in corridor means free of obstacles
 859            if len(corridor_forward_coordinates) == 0:
 860                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = z_max
 861            else:
 862                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = np.min(corridor_forward_coordinates)
 863
 864            if front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor >= min_clearance:
 865                valid_corridors.append({
 866                    "x_center": lat_c,
 867                    "clearance": front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor,
 868                })
 869
 870        def corridor_cost(c):
 871            """
 872            Score one valid corridor by distance from the forward axis.
 873
 874            Args:
 875                c:
 876                    Dictionary with ``x_center`` and ``clearance`` entries.
 877
 878            Returns:
 879                Non-negative lateral cost in meters. Smaller is preferred.
 880            """
 881            lateral_cost   = abs(c["x_center"] - 0.0)  # prefer corridors near center of robot fov (x=0 in camera frame)
 882
 883            return lateral_cost
 884        
 885        if len(valid_corridors) == 0:
 886            rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid virtual corridor for passability check.")
 887            # there is no virtual corridor available. you cannot consider in front of the robot as coridor. because there may be no passable corridor at all
 888            return None
 889        
 890        best_corridor = min(valid_corridors, key=corridor_cost) # it iterates over the list of dicts and passes each dict to corridor_cost
 891
 892        rospy.loginfo(f"Virtual corridor center defined at x: {best_corridor['x_center']:.3f} m in camera frame")
 893        return best_corridor['x_center']
 894    
 895
 896    def find_a_virtual_corridor(self, z_min, z_max, min_clearance):
 897        """
 898        Search the full depth image for a clear robot-width corridor.
 899
 900        Depth pixels in the requested range are back-projected, filtered by the
 901        normal/outlier/connected-component pipeline, transformed to the robot
 902        frame, and passed to the sliding-window corridor search.
 903
 904        Args:
 905            z_min:
 906                Nearest depth included in the search, in meters.
 907
 908            z_max:
 909                Farthest depth included in the search, in meters.
 910
 911            min_clearance:
 912                Required obstacle-free distance in meters.
 913
 914        Returns:
 915            A tuple ``(center, image)``. ``center`` is the selected lateral
 916            coordinate in the corridor frame, ``0.0`` when filtering finds no
 917            obstacles, or ``None`` when obstacles leave no valid candidate.
 918            ``image`` is the passability visualization.
 919
 920        Notes:
 921            An empty point cloud is interpreted as open space within the
 922            requested depth interval, so the forward axis is selected.
 923        """
 924        rospy.loginfo("Finding virtual corridor for passability check.")
 925       
 926
 927        # run passability check for full width of image to find a virtual corridor
 928
 929        valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, _ = backproject_depth_to_points(
 930            self.depth_image, self.fx, self.fy, self.cx, self.cy,
 931            max_depth=z_max, min_depth=z_min,
 932            subsample=self.subsample, roi_polygon=None
 933        )
 934        
 935        if len(valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) == 0:
 936            rospy.logwarn("No valid depth points after back-projection. Cannot define virtual corridor. but it is also possible that there is no points at all because entire region in front is free because of small depth range. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
 937            x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
 938            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, self.color_image
 939        else:
 940            corridor_mask_camera_frame = (
 941                valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[:, 1] > -self.robot_height_above_camera_level
 942            )
 943            #we are in camera frame so y down is positive. so we check if points are below the camera height (which means above the ground) by checking if y is greater than -robot_height_above_camera_level. level of camera is 0 in camera frame, and ground is at positive in camera frame. 
 944            # no image cropping. we need to check entire image for passability. 
 945            corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
 946            corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
 947            
 948            _, image, final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = self.passability_checker.run(
 949                self.depth_image,
 950                self.color_image,
 951                corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
 952                corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
 953                z_max
 954            )
 955
 956            if final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame is not None and len(final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) > 0:
 957                final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = (self.R_rc @ final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame.T).T + self.t_rc 
 958                # Keep only ground-plane components. Project to ground plane (robot X–Y)
 959                final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame[:, :2]  # Extract 2D points (x, y)
 960                # donot use the value of front clearance directly because corridor is not defined yet.  this front clerance is for full width of image
 961                # we need to find a virtual corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
 962                
 963
 964                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = self.find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance)
 965                #x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame value can be None or a float value. if it is None, it means no valid corridor is found. if it is a float value, it means the x center of the virtual corridor in the corridor frame is at that value. positive value means right side of the robot and negative value means left side of the robot. and 0 means directly in front of the robot.
 966            else: # in this case, consider image center as virtual corridor center
 967                rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid points after filtering for virtual corridor definition. This is possible that there is no points left after filtering, means entire region in front is free. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
 968                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
 969            
 970            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, image
 971
 972    def relative_robot_motion(self):
 973        """
 974        Compute robot motion since the current corridor was defined.
 975
 976        Returns:
 977            A tuple ``(R, t)``. ``R`` is the planar rotation from the corridor
 978            definition orientation to the current orientation, and ``t`` is
 979            current translation expressed in the definition frame.
 980
 981        Notes:
 982            Yaw difference is wrapped to ``[-pi, pi]`` before constructing the
 983            rotation matrix.
 984        """
 985
 986        dx_world = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 987        dy_world = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 988        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
 989        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
 990
 991        # Rotation matrix (start -> current)
 992        R = np.array([
 993            [ np.cos(delta_yaw), -np.sin(delta_yaw)],
 994            [ np.sin(delta_yaw),  np.cos(delta_yaw)]
 995        ])
 996
 997        R_world_to_R0 = np.array([
 998            [ np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)],
 999            [-np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)]
1000        ])
1001
1002        t = R_world_to_R0 @ np.array([dx_world, dy_world])
1003        return R, t
1004
1005    def propagate_corridor_point(self, corridor_point_R0,R, t):
1006        """
1007        Propagate a fixed corridor point into the current robot frame.
1008
1009        Args:
1010            corridor_point_R0:
1011                Two-element corridor point expressed in the robot frame at
1012                corridor-definition time.
1013
1014            R:
1015                Current planar rotation relative to the definition frame, as
1016                returned by :meth:`relative_robot_motion`.
1017
1018            t:
1019                Current planar translation in the definition frame.
1020
1021        Returns:
1022            Two-element ``[forward, lateral]`` point in the current robot
1023            frame.
1024        """
1025
1026        # Extract x,z (planar)
1027        p0 = np.array([
1028            corridor_point_R0[0],
1029            corridor_point_R0[1]
1030        ])
1031
1032        # Inverse robot motion
1033        p_now = R.T @ (p0 - t)
1034
1035        return p_now  # [X_forward, Y_lateral] in robot frame
1036    
1037    def project_to_pixel(self, P_cam):
1038        """
1039        Project one camera-frame point into image coordinates.
1040
1041        Args:
1042            P_cam:
1043                Three-element ``(X, Y, Z)`` camera-frame point in meters.
1044
1045        Returns:
1046            Integer ``(u, v)`` pixel coordinates, or ``None`` when the point is
1047            on or behind the camera plane.
1048        """
1049        X, Y, Z = P_cam
1050        if Z <= 0:
1051            return None
1052        u = int(self.fx * X / Z + self.cx)
1053        v = int(self.fy * Y / Z + self.cy)
1054        return (u, v)
1055
1056
1057    def run(self):
1058        """
1059        Define, propagate, and evaluate corridors until ROS shuts down.
1060
1061        On activation, the loop first defines a corridor from detected door
1062        geometry. A later traversal request can replace it with a virtual
1063        corridor selected from the visible free space. Each iteration uses
1064        odometry to express the fixed corridor in the current robot frame,
1065        chooses either corridor or local passability mode, filters the
1066        relevant RGB-D points, and publishes clearance and alignment data.
1067
1068        The traversal trigger is latched after the original corridor first
1069        provides enough clearance through and beyond the door. Optional
1070        visualization projects the evaluated corridor boundaries back into the
1071        color image.
1072
1073        Raises:
1074            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
1075                If a generated visualization cannot be converted to a ROS
1076                image outside the guarded visualization-publish block.
1077
1078        Notes:
1079            This is a blocking node loop. Subscriber callbacks only cache
1080            state; all expensive point-cloud work is performed here at the
1081            configured five-hertz rate.
1082        """
1083        while not rospy.is_shutdown():
1084            if not self.active: # node inactive, skip processing. node will be activated when door state is open_left or open_right and 
1085                #de activated when traversal done signal is received
1086                self.rate.sleep()
1087                continue
1088            
1089            # this is to wait until first time data is ready after activation
1090            if not self.first_time_data_ready_after_node_activation(): # if data not ready, wait
1091                self.rate.sleep()
1092                continue
1093
1094            
1095            # because ros subscriber callbacks and main loop are in different threads, it is possible that during main loop execution 
1096            # new data could come in self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node. but it is okay because the new data will be used in next iteration of main loop.
1097            # but we cannot use self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node directly here because it may change during execution of this main loop iteration.
1098            # so we use a local variable to store its value at the start of this iteration.
1099            if self.trigger_traversal_node:# once traversal node is triggered, it should remain triggered until deactivation. and only makes sense to 
1100                # consider the value from call back if traversal node is triggered. its fine that, setting trigger_traversal_node to true doesnt mean value will be available at 
1101                # first iteration itself. because in that case we can wait for next iteration to get the value. because subscriber cb will only be called when new data arrives.
1102                # so this if check block avoid setting type_of_passability_check to default 0 when trigger_traversal_node is true and requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node is not yet set by callback.
1103                type_of_passability_check = self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node
1104
1105            
1106
1107            # corridor definition stage. run only once when requested by frame detection node or traversal node. for frame detection node, it will be requested when door state is open. for traversal node, it can be requested anytime after activation when traversal node needs to redefine corridor based on updated robot pose
1108            if self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection:
1109
1110                self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition = self.current_yaw  # store the yaw at corridor definition time

1615def main():
1616    """
1617    Start the ROS corridor-passability node.
1618
1619    The function initializes ROS, creates :class:`PassabilityCheckerNode`, and
1620    enters its blocking processing loop.
1621
1622    Raises:
1623        rospy.ROSInterruptException:
1624            If ROS interrupts the node while it is running.
1625    """
1626    rospy.init_node("check_if_corridor_is_passable")
1627    node = PassabilityCheckerNode()
1628    rospy.loginfo("Check if corridor is passable node started.")
1629    node.run()
1630
1631
1632if __name__ == "__main__":
1633    main()
class PassabilityCheckerNode: 
  29class PassabilityCheckerNode:
  30    """
  31    Define traversable corridors and monitor their obstacle clearance.
  32
  33    The node is activated by a door-opening result. It combines the detected
  34    door geometry, aligned RGB-D data, camera-to-robot extrinsics, and odometry
  35    to build a corridor in a fixed reference frame. As the robot moves, the
  36    stored corridor is propagated into the current robot frame before the next
  37    clearance measurement is published to the traversal controller.
  38
  39    The same processing loop can also perform short-range, robot-centric
  40    checks and can search the visible scene for a virtual corridor when the
  41    original door corridor is no longer usable.
  42
  43    Attributes:
  44        active:
  45            Whether image and odometry processing is enabled.
  46
  47        color_image:
  48            Latest BGR color frame, or ``None`` before one is received.
  49
  50        depth_image:
  51            Latest aligned depth image in meters.
  52
  53        fx:
  54            Camera focal length along the image x axis, in pixels.
  55
  56        R_rc:
  57            Rotation matrix that maps camera-frame vectors into the robot
  58            ``trunk`` frame.
  59
  60        t_rc:
  61            Camera origin expressed in the robot frame, in meters.
  62
  63        requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node:
  64            Requested mode: ``0`` disables checks, ``1`` checks the stored
  65            corridor, and ``2`` checks the space directly ahead.
  66
  67        corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis:
  68            Current signed distance to the corridor midpoint, measured along
  69            the corridor axis in meters.
  70
  71        passability_checker:
  72            Point-cloud filtering pipeline used to find the nearest obstacle.
  73    """
  74
  75    def __init__(self):
  76        """
  77        Initialize corridor state, parameters, and ROS interfaces.
  78
  79        The constructor creates the always-on control subscribers and result
  80        publishers. High-bandwidth image topics and odometry remain
  81        unsubscribed until a suitable door state activates the node. Finally,
  82        the camera extrinsics are read from TF.
  83
  84        Raises:
  85            tf2_ros.LookupException:
  86                If the requested camera transform is unavailable.
  87
  88            tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
  89                If TF cannot connect the two requested frames.
  90
  91            tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
  92                If TF cannot provide a transform at the requested time.
  93
  94        Notes:
  95            The ROS node itself is initialized by :func:`main`, before this
  96            class is constructed.
  97        """
  98        self.enable_visualization = rospy.get_param("~enable_visualization", False)
  99        self.color_topic = rospy.get_param("~color_topic", "/camera/color/image_raw")
 100        self.depth_topic = rospy.get_param("~depth_topic", "/camera/aligned_depth_to_color/image_raw")
 101        self.camera_info_topic = rospy.get_param("~camera_info_topic", "/camera/color/camera_info")
 102        self.bridge = CvBridge()
 103        ns = "~passabilility_check"
 104        # ---- State ----
 105        self.active = False
 106        self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection = False
 107        self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node = None
 108        self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node = None
 109        self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node = None
 110        self.plane_info_distance_m = None
 111        self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame = None
 112        self.x_corridor_center_cam_first_time = None
 113        # Additional state for traversal-requested corridor definition and publishing
 114        self.define_new_corridor_req_from_traversal = False
 115        self.corridor_middle_point_depth_from_traversal = None
 116        self.virtual_corridor_definition_finished = False
 117        self.clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor = None
 118        self.corridor_middle_point_depth_first_time_camera_frame = None
 119
 120
 121        # Odometry
 122        self.start_pose_at_node_activation = None
 123        self.start_yaw_at_node_activation = None
 124        self.current_pose = None
 125        self.current_yaw = None
 126
 127        #dynamic values
 128        self.corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis = None
 129        self.x_corridor_center_cam_dynamic = None
 130
 131        # Latest sensor data
 132        self.color_image = None
 133        self.depth_image = None
 134        self.latest_info = None 
 135        self.fx = self.fy = self.cx = self.cy = None
 136
 137        # ---- Subscribers (conditional) ----
 138        self.color_sub = None
 139        self.depth_sub = None
 140        self.info_sub = None
 141        self.odom_sub = None

 147        self.maximum_depth_beyond_corridor_center_point_for_back_projection = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/back_proj_params/maximum_depth_beyond_corridor_center_point", 1.5)  # meters
 148        self.subsample = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/back_proj_params/subsample", 2)
 149

 151        self.minimum_depth_for_back_projection_local_passability_check = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/back_proj_params/minimum_depth_local_passability_check", 0.05)  # meters
 152        self.maximum_depth_for_back_projection_local_passability_check = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/back_proj_params/maximum_depth_local_passability_check", 0.5)  # meters
 153        self.robot_height_above_camera_level = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/traversal_params/robot_height_above_camera_level", 0.5)  # meters
 154        #pass ability decision parameters

 158        self.robot_width = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/traversal_params/robot_width", 0.45)  # meters ,robot  width
 159        self.robot_length = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/traversal_params/robot_length", 0.7)  # meters

 161        self.door_frame_margin = rospy.get_param(f"{ns}/traversal_params/door_frame_margin", 0.05)  # meters

 200        rospy.Subscriber(

 225        #result publishers

 255        self.passability_view_pub = rospy.Publisher(

 261        # Passability checker instance
 262        self.passability_checker = Passability_checker()
 263        self.rate = rospy.Rate(5)  # 5 Hz decision loop
 264
 265        self.R_rc, self.t_rc = self.get_camera_extrinsics_tf()

 269    # -----------------------------
 270    # Activation logic called upon door state changes
 271    # only update states, store data and activation/deactivation of camera subscriptions
 272    # call backs shall be non blocking and lightweight
 273    # -----------------------------
 274
 275    def get_camera_extrinsics_tf(self,
 276                                robot_frame="trunk",
 277                                camera_frame="realsense_d455_optical_frame"
 278                                ):
 279        """
 280        Read the camera pose in the robot frame from TF.
 281
 282        The returned transform maps an optical-frame point ``p_c`` to the
 283        robot frame as ``p_r = R_rc @ p_c + t_rc``. The camera optical axes are
 284        right, down, and forward; the robot axes are forward, left, and up.
 285
 286        Args:
 287            robot_frame:
 288                Target robot frame in which points should be expressed.
 289
 290            camera_frame:
 291                Source optical frame attached to the depth camera.
 292
 293        Returns:
 294            A tuple ``(R_rc, t_rc)`` containing a ``3 x 3`` rotation matrix and
 295            a three-element translation vector in meters.
 296
 297        Raises:
 298            tf2_ros.LookupException:
 299                If no transform is available for the named frames.
 300
 301            tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
 302                If the TF tree cannot connect the frames.
 303
 304            tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
 305                If TF cannot satisfy the requested timestamp.
 306
 307        Notes:
 308            This method is intended to run once after the robot and camera
 309            frames have been published. It waits up to five seconds in the
 310            initial availability check.
 311
 312        """
 313
 314
 315        tf_buffer = tf2_ros.Buffer()
 316        tf_listener = tf2_ros.TransformListener(tf_buffer)
 317
 318        rospy.loginfo("Waiting for TF %s -> %s",
 319                    robot_frame, camera_frame)
 320
 321        # Wait until TF is available
 322        tf_buffer.can_transform(
 323            robot_frame,
 324            camera_frame,
 325            rospy.Time(0),
 326            rospy.Duration(5.0)
 327        )
 328
 329        transform = tf_buffer.lookup_transform(
 330            robot_frame,
 331            camera_frame,
 332            rospy.Time(0)
 333        )
 334
 335        # Translation
 336        t = transform.transform.translation
 337        t_rc = np.array([t.x, t.y, t.z])
 338
 339        # Rotation (quaternion → matrix)
 340        q = transform.transform.rotation
 341        quat = [q.x, q.y, q.z, q.w]
 342        R_rc = R.from_quat(quat).as_matrix()
 343
 344        rospy.loginfo("Camera extrinsics loaded from TF")
 345        print("R_rc =\n", R_rc)
 346        test = np.array([0, 0, 1])  # camera forward
 347        print("Camera forward in robot frame:", R_rc @ test)
 348
 349
 350
 351        return R_rc, t_rc
 352
 353
 354    def _activate_node_cb(self, msg):
 355        """
 356        Activate passability processing for an eligible door state.
 357
 358        Args:
 359            msg:
 360                ROS ``String`` containing the detected door state.
 361
 362        Notes:
 363            ``open_left``, ``open_right``, ``No_door_plane_detected``, and
 364            ``no_frame_detected`` start a new cycle. The first accepted state is
 365            retained as the basis for corridor definition.
 366        """
 367        if msg.data in ["open_left", "open_right", "No_door_plane_detected", "no_frame_detected"]: # one time activation on these states
 368            if not self.active:
 369                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: activated")
 370                self.active = True
 371                #to create subscriptions
 372                self.activate_camera()
 373                self.get_odom()
 374                # store the door open status only once at activation
 375                self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data 
 376                self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection = True  # to define new corridor on next run
 377                
 378            
 379
 380    def _deactivate_node_cb(self, msg):
 381        """
 382        End the active passability cycle after traversal completes.
 383
 384        Args:
 385            msg:
 386                ROS ``Bool`` message. Only a true value causes deactivation.
 387
 388        Notes:
 389            The callback unregisters conditional subscribers, clears
 390            cycle-specific geometry, and asks the door detector to start its
 391            next detection cycle.
 392        """
 393        if msg.data:  # only deactivate on True
 394            if self.active:
 395                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: deactivated by traversal done signal")
 396                self.deactivate_camera()
 397                self.deactivate_odom()
 398            self.active = False
 399            self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection = False
 400            self.trigger_traversal_node = False # to deactivate traversal node. because door is already traversed
 401            # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 402            self.x_corridor_center_cam_first_time = None
 403            self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node = None
 404            self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node = 1 # reset to default 1 for corridor
 405            self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node = None
 406            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node = None
 407            self.plane_info_distance_m = None
 408            self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame = None
 409            self.virtual_corridor_definition_finished = False
 410            self.corridor_middle_point_depth_from_traversal = None
 411            self.retrigger_door_detection_node_pub.publish(True) # to retrigger door detection node for next detection and traversal cycle
 412
 413
 414

 416    # -----------------------------
 417    # Conditional subscriptions
 418    # -----------------------------
 419    def activate_camera(self):
 420        """
 421        Subscribe to the color, aligned-depth, and camera-info topics.
 422
 423        Notes:
 424            Each subscriber is created only if it is not already active, so
 425            repeated activation requests are safe.
 426        """
 427        if self.color_sub is None:
 428            self.color_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 429                self.color_topic,
 430                Image,
 431                self._color_cb,
 432                queue_size=1
 433            )
 434        if self.depth_sub is None:
 435            self.depth_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 436                self.depth_topic,
 437                Image,
 438                self._depth_cb,
 439                queue_size=1
 440            )
 441        if self.info_sub is None:
 442            self.info_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 443                self.camera_info_topic,
 444                CameraInfo,
 445                self._info_cb,
 446                queue_size=1
 447            )
 448    
 449    def deactivate_camera(self):
 450        """
 451        Unregister camera subscribers and discard their cached data.
 452
 453        Notes:
 454            Clearing the cached frames forces a later activation cycle to wait
 455            for fresh camera data instead of reusing an old observation.
 456        """
 457        for sub in [self.color_sub, self.depth_sub, self.info_sub]:
 458            if sub is not None:
 459                sub.unregister()
 460
 461        self.color_sub = None
 462        self.depth_sub = None
 463        self.info_sub = None
 464
 465
 466        # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 467        self.color_image = None
 468        self.depth_image = None
 469        self.latest_info = None
 470    
 471        
 472
 473    def get_odom(self):
 474        """
 475        Subscribe to robot odometry when it is not already active.
 476
 477        Notes:
 478            The first odometry sample received after subscription establishes
 479            the node-activation reference pose.
 480        """
 481        if self.odom_sub is None:
 482            self.odom_sub = rospy.Subscriber(
 483                "/odom_bridge_output",
 484                Odometry,
 485                self._odom_callback,
 486                queue_size=1
 487            )
 488
 489    def deactivate_odom(self):
 490        """
 491        Unregister odometry and clear all cached planar poses.
 492
 493        Notes:
 494            Both the current pose and the activation reference are reset so
 495            that the next cycle starts in a new local reference frame.
 496        """
 497        if self.odom_sub is not None:
 498            self.odom_sub.unregister()
 499            self.odom_sub = None
 500        # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
 501        self.start_pose_at_node_activation = None
 502        self.start_yaw_at_node_activation = None
 503        self.current_pose = None
 504        self.current_yaw = None
 505
 506    # -----------------------------
 507    # Callbacks (store only!)
 508    # -----------------------------
 509    def _color_cb(self, color_msg):
 510        """
 511        Convert and cache the latest ROS color image.
 512
 513        Args:
 514            color_msg:
 515                ROS ``Image`` converted to an OpenCV BGR image with
 516                ``CvBridge``.
 517
 518        Raises:
 519            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
 520                If the message cannot be converted as ``bgr8``.
 521        """
 522        self.color_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(color_msg, "bgr8")
 523
 524    def _depth_cb(self, depth_msg):
 525        """
 526        Convert and cache the latest depth image in meters.
 527
 528        Args:
 529            depth_msg:
 530                ROS ``Image`` containing millimeter ``16UC1``/``mono16`` depth
 531                or a floating-point depth representation.
 532
 533        Raises:
 534            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
 535                If the ROS image cannot be converted.
 536        """
 537        img = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(depth_msg, "passthrough")
 538
 539        if depth_msg.encoding in ("16UC1", "mono16"):
 540            depth_mm = img.astype(np.uint16)
 541            depth_m = depth_mm.astype(np.float32) / 1000.0
 542        else:
 543            depth_m = img.astype(np.float32)
 544
 545        self.depth_image = depth_m
 546
 547    def _info_cb(self, info_msg: CameraInfo):
 548        """
 549        Cache camera calibration from the first camera-info message.
 550
 551        Args:
 552            info_msg:
 553                ROS ``CameraInfo`` whose intrinsic matrix follows the standard
 554                row-major ``K`` layout.
 555
 556        Notes:
 557            Calibration is treated as constant during a run; later messages
 558            are ignored.
 559        """
 560        # storing the camera intrinsics only once. it will not change during runtime
 561        if self.latest_info is None:
 562            self.latest_info = info_msg
 563            K = info_msg.K
 564            self.fx, self.fy = K[0], K[4]
 565            self.cx, self.cy = K[2], K[5]
 566            rospy.loginfo("Camera intrinsics received and stored.")
 567    
 568    def _mid_frame_x_px_cb(self, msg):
 569        """
 570        Store the first valid door-frame midpoint pixel of an active cycle.
 571
 572        Args:
 573            msg:
 574                ROS ``Int32`` containing the horizontal image coordinate.
 575
 576        Notes:
 577            Non-positive values and samples received while inactive are
 578            ignored.
 579        """
 580        if msg.data <= 0: # invalid pixel
 581            return
 582        # only update if not set. which means take only first valid pixel after activation
 583        # checking self.active will make sure we get door depth and mid frame only when door state is open
 584        if self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node is None and self.active:
 585            self.mid_frame_x_px_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data
 586
 587    def _plane_info_cb(self, msg):
 588        """
 589        Store the first valid detected door-plane measurement.
 590
 591        Args:
 592            msg:
 593                ROS ``Twist`` used as a compact container. ``linear.x`` is
 594                plane distance in meters, while ``angular.(x, y, z)`` contains
 595                the camera-frame normal.
 596
 597        Notes:
 598            A non-positive distance is invalid. Only the first valid sample in
 599            an active cycle is retained.
 600        """
 601        # plane info is published as Twist for simplicity, where:
 602        # linear.x = distance_m, angular.x = plane_norm_x, angular.y = plane_norm_y, angular.z = plane_norm_z
 603        if msg.linear.x <= 0.0: # invalid distance
 604            return
 605        if self.plane_info_distance_m is None and self.active:
 606            self.plane_info_distance_m = msg.linear.x
 607            self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame = np.array([msg.angular.x, msg.angular.y, msg.angular.z])
 608            rospy.loginfo(f"Received plane info from frame detection node: distance {self.plane_info_distance_m:.2f} m, normal vector {self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame}")
 609
 610    def _request_local_passability_check_cb(self, msg):
 611        """
 612        Store the passability mode requested by the traversal controller.
 613
 614        Args:
 615            msg:
 616                ROS ``UInt8``: ``0`` disables checking, ``1`` requests the
 617                corridor mode, and ``2`` requests the local mode.
 618        """
 619        if msg.data in [0, 1, 2]: # 1 for corridor , 2 for local
 620            self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node = msg.data
 621    
 622    def _request_new_corridor_definition_cb(self, msg):
 623        """
 624        Record a traversal-side request for a virtual corridor.
 625
 626        Args:
 627            msg:
 628                ROS ``Twist`` used as a request container. A truthy
 629                ``linear.x`` enables the request and ``linear.y`` supplies the
 630                desired corridor-midpoint depth in meters.
 631
 632        Notes:
 633            Requests are accepted only while the node is active.
 634        """
 635        if msg.linear.x:  # only activate on True
 636            if self.active:
 637                rospy.loginfo("PassabilityChecker: New corridor definition requested by traversal node")
 638                self.define_new_corridor_req_from_traversal = True  # to define new corridor on next run
 639                self.corridor_middle_point_depth_from_traversal = msg.linear.y  # to define new corridor based on this depth
 640
 641
 642    
 643    def _door_depth_cb(self, msg):
 644        """
 645        Store the first valid detected door depth of an active cycle.
 646
 647        Args:
 648            msg:
 649                ROS ``Float32`` containing depth in meters.
 650
 651        Notes:
 652            Non-positive samples and later samples from the same cycle are
 653            ignored.
 654        """
 655        if msg.data <= 0.0: # invalid depth
 656            return
 657        # only update if not set. which means take only first valid depth after activation
 658        # checking self.active will make sure we get door depth and mid frame only when door state is open
 659        if self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node is None and self.active:
 660            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node = msg.data
 661
 662    def _odom_callback(self, msg):
 663        """
 664        Cache planar odometry and establish the activation reference pose.
 665
 666        Args:
 667            msg:
 668                ROS ``Odometry`` containing the robot position and quaternion
 669                orientation.
 670
 671        Notes:
 672            The first sample after activation is stored separately so later
 673            displacement can be measured relative to the start of the cycle.
 674        """
 675        p = msg.pose.pose.position
 676        q = msg.pose.pose.orientation
 677
 678
 679        self.current_pose = (p.x, p.y)
 680
 681        quat = [q.x, q.y, q.z, q.w]
 682        _, _, yaw = euler_from_quaternion(quat)
 683        self.current_yaw = yaw
 684        # store the start pose and yaw at activation.run only once
 685        if self.start_pose_at_node_activation is None:
 686            self.start_pose_at_node_activation = (p.x, p.y)
 687            self.start_yaw_at_node_activation = yaw
 688        
 689
