 691    # -----------------------------
 692    # Check if image data is available
 693    # -----------------------------
 694
 695    def first_time_data_ready_after_node_activation(self):
 696        """
 697        Check whether initial corridor-definition inputs are available.
 698
 699        Returns:
 700            ``True`` when color, depth, intrinsics, door state, door depth, and
 701            the activation pose have all been received; otherwise ``False``.
 702        """
 703        return (
 704            self.color_image is not None and
 705            self.depth_image is not None and
 706            self.fx is not None and
 707            self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node is not None and
 708            self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node is not None and
 709            self.start_pose_at_node_activation is not None and
 710            self.start_yaw_at_node_activation is not None
 711        )
 712
 713    def get_forward_displacement_since_start(self):
 714        """
 715        Measure motion along the corridor-definition heading.
 716
 717        Returns:
 718            Signed displacement in meters along the yaw recorded when the
 719            current corridor was defined.
 720
 721        Notes:
 722            Projecting world translation onto a fixed heading keeps the result
 723            independent of later yaw corrections.
 724        """
 725
 726        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 727        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 728
 729        return dx * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 730    
 731    def get_lateral_displacement_since_start(self):
 732        """
 733        Measure motion perpendicular to the corridor-definition heading.
 734
 735        Returns:
 736            Signed lateral displacement in meters in the reference frame that
 737            was active when the corridor was defined.
 738
 739        Notes:
 740            The sign follows the left-handed lateral basis produced by
 741            ``(-sin(yaw), cos(yaw))``.
 742        """
 743
 744        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 745        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 746
 747        return -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 748    
 749    def calculate_dynamic_x_corridor_center_in_cameraframe(self):
 750        """
 751        Estimate the apparent lateral corridor shift from odometry.
 752
 753        Translation perpendicular to the initial heading and the image shift
 754        caused by accumulated yaw are added together.
 755
 756        Returns:
 757            Estimated horizontal corridor-center displacement in meters.
 758
 759        Notes:
 760            The rotational term uses the current distance to the corridor
 761            midpoint, so the estimate grows as heading error acts over a longer
 762            viewing distance.
 763        """
 764
 765        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 766        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 767        
 768        #translation effect
 769        # Project displacement onto perpendicular to initial heading
 770        lateral_displacement = -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
 771
 772        #rotation effect
 773        # rotation effect
 774        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
 775        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
 776
 777        rotation_shift = (self.corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis * np.tan(delta_yaw))
 778    
 779        
 780        rospy.loginfo(f"start pose is {self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition} and current pose is {self.current_pose}   Lateral displacement from start: {lateral_displacement:.3f} m   Rotation shift: {rotation_shift:.3f} m")
 781        
 782        
 783        return (
 784        lateral_displacement
 785        + rotation_shift
 786    )
 787
 788    
 789
 790    def find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(self, final_points_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance):
 791        """
 792        Slide a robot-width window and choose a clear centerline.
 793
 794        Candidate centers span the camera field of view in corridor
 795        coordinates. A candidate is valid when its nearest obstacle is beyond
 796        ``min_clearance``. Among valid candidates, the center closest to the
 797        robot's current forward axis is preferred.
 798
 799        Args:
 800            final_points_robot_frame:
 801                ``N x 2`` array of filtered obstacle points on the robot-frame
 802                ground plane, in meters.
 803
 804            z_max:
 805                Far search distance in meters. It defines the visible lateral
 806                span and is used as clearance when a candidate contains no
 807                obstacle points.
 808
 809            min_clearance:
 810                Minimum acceptable forward clearance in meters.
 811
 812        Returns:
 813            Lateral center coordinate of the best corridor in meters, or
 814            ``None`` when no robot-width candidate meets the clearance
 815            requirement.
 816
 817        Notes:
 818            Candidate width includes the configured robot half-width and safety
 819            margin.
 820        """
 821        # find best corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
 822        # final points are in robot frame
 823
 824
 825        forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 826        lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 827
 828
 829        H, W = self.depth_image.shape
 830        x_edge_camera_frame = (W / 2.0) * z_max / self.fx
 831
 832        left_edge_camera_frame  = np.array([-x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
 833        right_edge_camera_frame = np.array([ x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
 834
 835        left_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ left_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
 836        right_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ right_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
 837
 838        left_edge_corridor_frame = left_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 839        right_edge_corridor_frame = right_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
 840
 841        lat_min_corridor_frame = min(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
 842        lat_max_corridor_frame = max(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
 843        slide_centers_corridor_frame = np.arange(lat_min_corridor_frame + self.half_width, lat_max_corridor_frame - self.half_width, self.slide_step_x_direction)
 844        # because lateral min and max depends on entire image,not just on the obstacle points. 
 845
 846        valid_corridors = []
 847
 848        for lat_c in slide_centers_corridor_frame:
 849            x_left  = lat_c - self.half_width
 850            x_right = lat_c + self.half_width
 851
 852            corridor_mask = (
 853                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame > x_left) &
 854                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame < x_right)
 855            )
 856
 857            corridor_forward_coordinates = forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame[corridor_mask]
 858
 859            # no points in corridor means free of obstacles
 860            if len(corridor_forward_coordinates) == 0:
 861                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = z_max
 862            else:
 863                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = np.min(corridor_forward_coordinates)
 864
 865            if front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor >= min_clearance:
 866                valid_corridors.append({
 867                    "x_center": lat_c,
 868                    "clearance": front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor,
 869                })
 870
 871        def corridor_cost(c):
 872            """
 873            Score one valid corridor by distance from the forward axis.
 874
 875            Args:
 876                c:
 877                    Dictionary with ``x_center`` and ``clearance`` entries.
 878
 879            Returns:
 880                Non-negative lateral cost in meters. Smaller is preferred.
 881            """
 882            lateral_cost   = abs(c["x_center"] - 0.0)  # prefer corridors near center of robot fov (x=0 in camera frame)
 883
 884            return lateral_cost
 885        
 886        if len(valid_corridors) == 0:
 887            rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid virtual corridor for passability check.")
 888            # there is no virtual corridor available. you cannot consider in front of the robot as coridor. because there may be no passable corridor at all
 889            return None
 890        
 891        best_corridor = min(valid_corridors, key=corridor_cost) # it iterates over the list of dicts and passes each dict to corridor_cost
 892
 893        rospy.loginfo(f"Virtual corridor center defined at x: {best_corridor['x_center']:.3f} m in camera frame")
 894        return best_corridor['x_center']
 895    
 896
 897    def find_a_virtual_corridor(self, z_min, z_max, min_clearance):
 898        """
 899        Search the full depth image for a clear robot-width corridor.
 900
 901        Depth pixels in the requested range are back-projected, filtered by the
 902        normal/outlier/connected-component pipeline, transformed to the robot
 903        frame, and passed to the sliding-window corridor search.
 904
 905        Args:
 906            z_min:
 907                Nearest depth included in the search, in meters.
 908
 909            z_max:
 910                Farthest depth included in the search, in meters.
 911
 912            min_clearance:
 913                Required obstacle-free distance in meters.
 914
 915        Returns:
 916            A tuple ``(center, image)``. ``center`` is the selected lateral
 917            coordinate in the corridor frame, ``0.0`` when filtering finds no
 918            obstacles, or ``None`` when obstacles leave no valid candidate.
 919            ``image`` is the passability visualization.
 920
 921        Notes:
 922            An empty point cloud is interpreted as open space within the
 923            requested depth interval, so the forward axis is selected.
 924        """
 925        rospy.loginfo("Finding virtual corridor for passability check.")
 926       
 927
 928        # run passability check for full width of image to find a virtual corridor
 929
 930        valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, _ = backproject_depth_to_points(
 931            self.depth_image, self.fx, self.fy, self.cx, self.cy,
 932            max_depth=z_max, min_depth=z_min,
 933            subsample=self.subsample, roi_polygon=None
 934        )
 935        
 936        if len(valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) == 0:
 937            rospy.logwarn("No valid depth points after back-projection. Cannot define virtual corridor. but it is also possible that there is no points at all because entire region in front is free because of small depth range. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
 938            x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
 939            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, self.color_image
 940        else:
 941            corridor_mask_camera_frame = (
 942                valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[:, 1] > -self.robot_height_above_camera_level
 943            )
 944            #we are in camera frame so y down is positive. so we check if points are below the camera height (which means above the ground) by checking if y is greater than -robot_height_above_camera_level. level of camera is 0 in camera frame, and ground is at positive in camera frame. 
 945            # no image cropping. we need to check entire image for passability. 
 946            corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
 947            corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
 948            
 949            _, image, final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = self.passability_checker.run(
 950                self.depth_image,
 951                self.color_image,
 952                corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
 953                corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
 954                z_max
 955            )
 956
 957            if final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame is not None and len(final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) > 0:
 958                final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = (self.R_rc @ final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame.T).T + self.t_rc 
 959                # Keep only ground-plane components. Project to ground plane (robot X–Y)
 960                final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame[:, :2]  # Extract 2D points (x, y)
 961                # donot use the value of front clearance directly because corridor is not defined yet.  this front clerance is for full width of image
 962                # we need to find a virtual corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
 963                
 964
 965                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = self.find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance)
 966                #x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame value can be None or a float value. if it is None, it means no valid corridor is found. if it is a float value, it means the x center of the virtual corridor in the corridor frame is at that value. positive value means right side of the robot and negative value means left side of the robot. and 0 means directly in front of the robot.
 967            else: # in this case, consider image center as virtual corridor center
 968                rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid points after filtering for virtual corridor definition. This is possible that there is no points left after filtering, means entire region in front is free. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
 969                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
 970            
 971            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, image
 972
 973    def relative_robot_motion(self):
 974        """
 975        Compute robot motion since the current corridor was defined.
 976
 977        Returns:
 978            A tuple ``(R, t)``. ``R`` is the planar rotation from the corridor
 979            definition orientation to the current orientation, and ``t`` is
 980            current translation expressed in the definition frame.
 981
 982        Notes:
 983            Yaw difference is wrapped to ``[-pi, pi]`` before constructing the
 984            rotation matrix.
 985        """
 986
 987        dx_world = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 988        dy_world = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 989        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
 990        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
 991
 992        # Rotation matrix (start -> current)
 993        R = np.array([
 994            [ np.cos(delta_yaw), -np.sin(delta_yaw)],
 995            [ np.sin(delta_yaw),  np.cos(delta_yaw)]
 996        ])
 997
 998        R_world_to_R0 = np.array([
 999            [ np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)],
1000            [-np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)]
1001        ])
1002
1003        t = R_world_to_R0 @ np.array([dx_world, dy_world])
1004        return R, t
1005
1006    def propagate_corridor_point(self, corridor_point_R0,R, t):
1007        """
1008        Propagate a fixed corridor point into the current robot frame.
1009
1010        Args:
1011            corridor_point_R0:
1012                Two-element corridor point expressed in the robot frame at
1013                corridor-definition time.
1014
1015            R:
1016                Current planar rotation relative to the definition frame, as
1017                returned by :meth:`relative_robot_motion`.
1018
1019            t:
1020                Current planar translation in the definition frame.
1021
1022        Returns:
1023            Two-element ``[forward, lateral]`` point in the current robot
1024            frame.
1025        """
1026
1027        # Extract x,z (planar)
1028        p0 = np.array([
1029            corridor_point_R0[0],
1030            corridor_point_R0[1]
1031        ])
1032
1033        # Inverse robot motion
1034        p_now = R.T @ (p0 - t)
1035
1036        return p_now  # [X_forward, Y_lateral] in robot frame
1037    
1038    def project_to_pixel(self, P_cam):
1039        """
1040        Project one camera-frame point into image coordinates.
1041
1042        Args:
1043            P_cam:
1044                Three-element ``(X, Y, Z)`` camera-frame point in meters.
1045
1046        Returns:
1047            Integer ``(u, v)`` pixel coordinates, or ``None`` when the point is
1048            on or behind the camera plane.
1049        """
1050        X, Y, Z = P_cam
1051        if Z <= 0:
1052            return None
1053        u = int(self.fx * X / Z + self.cx)
1054        v = int(self.fy * Y / Z + self.cy)
1055        return (u, v)
1056
1057
1058    def run(self):
1059        """
1060        Define, propagate, and evaluate corridors until ROS shuts down.
1061
1062        On activation, the loop first defines a corridor from detected door
1063        geometry. A later traversal request can replace it with a virtual
1064        corridor selected from the visible free space. Each iteration uses
1065        odometry to express the fixed corridor in the current robot frame,
1066        chooses either corridor or local passability mode, filters the
1067        relevant RGB-D points, and publishes clearance and alignment data.
1068
1069        The traversal trigger is latched after the original corridor first
1070        provides enough clearance through and beyond the door. Optional
1071        visualization projects the evaluated corridor boundaries back into the
1072        color image.
1073
1074        Raises:
1075            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
1076                If a generated visualization cannot be converted to a ROS
1077                image outside the guarded visualization-publish block.
1078
1079        Notes:
1080            This is a blocking node loop. Subscriber callbacks only cache
1081            state; all expensive point-cloud work is performed here at the
1082            configured five-hertz rate.
1083        """
1084        while not rospy.is_shutdown():
1085            if not self.active: # node inactive, skip processing. node will be activated when door state is open_left or open_right and 
1086                #de activated when traversal done signal is received
1087                self.rate.sleep()
1088                continue
1089            
1090            # this is to wait until first time data is ready after activation
1091            if not self.first_time_data_ready_after_node_activation(): # if data not ready, wait
1092                self.rate.sleep()
1093                continue
1094
1095            
1096            # because ros subscriber callbacks and main loop are in different threads, it is possible that during main loop execution 
1097            # new data could come in self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node. but it is okay because the new data will be used in next iteration of main loop.
1098            # but we cannot use self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node directly here because it may change during execution of this main loop iteration.
1099            # so we use a local variable to store its value at the start of this iteration.
1100            if self.trigger_traversal_node:# once traversal node is triggered, it should remain triggered until deactivation. and only makes sense to 
1101                # consider the value from call back if traversal node is triggered. its fine that, setting trigger_traversal_node to true doesnt mean value will be available at 
1102                # first iteration itself. because in that case we can wait for next iteration to get the value. because subscriber cb will only be called when new data arrives.
1103                # so this if check block avoid setting type_of_passability_check to default 0 when trigger_traversal_node is true and requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node is not yet set by callback.
1104                type_of_passability_check = self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node
1105
1106            
1107
1108            # corridor definition stage. run only once when requested by frame detection node or traversal node. for frame detection node, it will be requested when door state is open. for traversal node, it can be requested anytime after activation when traversal node needs to redefine corridor based on updated robot pose
1109            if self.define_new_corridor_req_from_frame_detection:
1110
1111                self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition = self.current_yaw  # store the yaw at corridor definition time
1112                self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition = self.current_pose  # store the pose at corridor definition time
1113                clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor = self.min_corridor_clearance_beyond_door_to_trigger_traversal_node #value is considering robot should pass through the door. this info is not from traversal node but from the parameter server because it is related to the door and corridor, not related to the robot pose which is updated in real time. so it should be a fixed value instead of dynamic value updated from traversal node
1114                
1115                # find the corridor based on frame detection node data(x_center_frame_first_time_camera_frame)
1116                self.corridor_middle_point_depth_first_time_camera_frame = self.door_depth_from_frame_detection_node
1117                    
1118                self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame /= np.linalg.norm(self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame) # normalize plane normal vector
1119                plane_info_norm_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame 
1120                rospy.loginfo(f"Plane normal in robot base frame: {plane_info_norm_robot_frame}")
1121                self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame = np.array([
1122                    plane_info_norm_robot_frame[0],   # X ( forward in robot base )
1123                    plane_info_norm_robot_frame[1]    # Y ( left in robot base )
1124                ]) # y component of the normal is ignored. because that describe the tilt of the plane which is not relevant for corridor definition. we only care about the normal direction parallel to the ground plane which is defined by x and z in robot base frame
1125                
1126                norm = np.linalg.norm(self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame)
1127                if norm < 1e-6:
1128                    raise ValueError("Plane normal is nearly vertical — cannot define corridor axis")
1129                self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame /= norm
1130
1131                
1132
1133                """
1134                # Ensure corridor axis points away from robot. After this: forward means “towards the corridor”
1135                if np.dot(self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame, Point_mid_frame_first_time_2d_robot_frame) < 0:
1136                    self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame *= -1.0
1137                """
1138
1139                self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame = np.array([
1140                                            -self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame[1],
1141                                            self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame[0]
1142                                        ])
1143                self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame /= np.linalg.norm(self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame)  # left or right direction parallel to the ground plane and perpendicular to the corridor forward direction
1144                
1145                # convert to 3d by adding z component. this is because we need to calculate the offset_3d_robot_frame in 3d space and then add it to the mid frame point in 3d space to get the corridor center point in 3d space. if we do the calculation in 2d space, we will lose the z component which is important for accurate corridor center point calculation in 3d space
1146                #lift axes to 3d just to calculate the offset in 3d space. because we need to consider the z component of the plane normal for accurate corridor center point calculation in 3d space. if we do the calculation in 2d space, we will lose the z component which is important for accurate corridor center point calculation in 3d space
1147                # but for the calculation of lateral error and forward error for passability check, we will consider only the x and y component of the corridor center point in robot frame because we are interested in the ground plane distance of the robot from the corridor center line. and for that we will project the robot position and corridor center point to the ground plane by ignoring the z component. because the z component may have noise and errors which can affect the accuracy of the forward and lateral error calculation for passability check. so for corridor center point calculation we will consider z component but for error calculation we will ignore z component by projecting to ground plane. this is a design choice to improve the robustness of the passability check against noise in depth data which can affect the accuracy of z component of corridor center point in robot frame.
1148
1149                
1150                corridor_lateral_3d_unit_vector_robot_frame = np.array([
1151                    self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame[0],
1152                    self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame[1],
1153                    0.0
1154                ]) # convert to 3d by adding z component. this is because we need to calculate the offset_3d_robot_frame in 3d space and then add it to the mid frame point in 3d space to get the corridor center point in 3d space. if we do the calculation in 2d space, we will lose the z component which is important for accurate corridor center point calculation in 3d space
1155                
1156
1157                rospy.loginfo(f"Corridor forward 2D unit vector: {self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame}, Corridor lateral 2D unit vector: {self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame}")
1158                
1159
1160                if self.door_status_from_frame_detection_node in ["open_left", "open_right"]: # fixed corridor. and corridor is defined only when door is open

1378            # but for the calculation of lateral error and forward error for passability check, we will consider only the x and y component of the corridor center point in robot frame because we are interested in the ground plane distance of the robot from the corridor center line. and for that we will project the robot position and corridor center point to the ground plane by ignoring the z component. because the z component may have noise and errors which can affect the accuracy of the forward and lateral error calculation for passability check. so for corridor center point calculation we will consider z component but for error calculation we will ignore z component by projecting to ground plane. this is a design choice to improve the robustness of the passability check against noise in depth data which can affect the accuracy of z component of corridor center point in robot frame.
1379            # corridor_forward_3d_unit_vector_robot_frame is created just for visualization
1380            corridor_forward_3d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now = np.array([
1381                corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now[0],
1382                corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now[1],
1383                0.0
1384            ])  
1385            
1386            corridor_lateral_3d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now = np.array([
1387                corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now[0],
1388                corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now[1],
1389                0.0
1390            ])

1395                )

1397            # this is value increase as robot go towards corridor. not a distance measure

Define traversable corridors and monitor their obstacle clearance.

The node is activated by a door-opening result. It combines the detected door geometry, aligned RGB-D data, camera-to-robot extrinsics, and odometry to build a corridor in a fixed reference frame. As the robot moves, the stored corridor is propagated into the current robot frame before the next clearance measurement is published to the traversal controller.

The same processing loop can also perform short-range, robot-centric checks and can search the visible scene for a virtual corridor when the original door corridor is no longer usable.

Attributes: active: Whether image and odometry processing is enabled.

color_image:
    Latest BGR color frame, or ``None`` before one is received.

depth_image:
    Latest aligned depth image in meters.

fx:
    Camera focal length along the image x axis, in pixels.

R_rc:
    Rotation matrix that maps camera-frame vectors into the robot
    ``trunk`` frame.

t_rc:
    Camera origin expressed in the robot frame, in meters.

requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node:
    Requested mode: ``0`` disables checks, ``1`` checks the stored
    corridor, and ``2`` checks the space directly ahead.

corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis:
    Current signed distance to the corridor midpoint, measured along
    the corridor axis in meters.

passability_checker:
    Point-cloud filtering pipeline used to find the nearest obstacle.

Initialize corridor state, parameters, and ROS interfaces.

The constructor creates the always-on control subscribers and result publishers. High-bandwidth image topics and odometry remain unsubscribed until a suitable door state activates the node. Finally, the camera extrinsics are read from TF.

Raises: tf2_ros.LookupException: If the requested camera transform is unavailable.

tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
    If TF cannot connect the two requested frames.

tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
    If TF cannot provide a transform at the requested time.

Notes: The ROS node itself is initialized by main(), before this class is constructed.

def get_camera_extrinsics_tf( self, robot_frame='trunk', camera_frame='realsense_d455_optical_frame'): 
275    def get_camera_extrinsics_tf(self,
276                                robot_frame="trunk",
277                                camera_frame="realsense_d455_optical_frame"
278                                ):
279        """
280        Read the camera pose in the robot frame from TF.
281
282        The returned transform maps an optical-frame point ``p_c`` to the
283        robot frame as ``p_r = R_rc @ p_c + t_rc``. The camera optical axes are
284        right, down, and forward; the robot axes are forward, left, and up.
285
286        Args:
287            robot_frame:
288                Target robot frame in which points should be expressed.
289
290            camera_frame:
291                Source optical frame attached to the depth camera.
292
293        Returns:
294            A tuple ``(R_rc, t_rc)`` containing a ``3 x 3`` rotation matrix and
295            a three-element translation vector in meters.
296
297        Raises:
298            tf2_ros.LookupException:
299                If no transform is available for the named frames.
300
301            tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
302                If the TF tree cannot connect the frames.
303
304            tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
305                If TF cannot satisfy the requested timestamp.
306
307        Notes:
308            This method is intended to run once after the robot and camera
309            frames have been published. It waits up to five seconds in the
310            initial availability check.
311
312        """
313
314
315        tf_buffer = tf2_ros.Buffer()
316        tf_listener = tf2_ros.TransformListener(tf_buffer)
317
318        rospy.loginfo("Waiting for TF %s -> %s",
319                    robot_frame, camera_frame)
320
321        # Wait until TF is available
322        tf_buffer.can_transform(
323            robot_frame,
324            camera_frame,
325            rospy.Time(0),
326            rospy.Duration(5.0)
327        )
328
329        transform = tf_buffer.lookup_transform(
330            robot_frame,
331            camera_frame,
332            rospy.Time(0)
333        )
334
335        # Translation
336        t = transform.transform.translation
337        t_rc = np.array([t.x, t.y, t.z])
338
339        # Rotation (quaternion → matrix)
340        q = transform.transform.rotation
341        quat = [q.x, q.y, q.z, q.w]
342        R_rc = R.from_quat(quat).as_matrix()
343
344        rospy.loginfo("Camera extrinsics loaded from TF")
345        print("R_rc =\n", R_rc)
346        test = np.array([0, 0, 1])  # camera forward
347        print("Camera forward in robot frame:", R_rc @ test)
348
349
350
351        return R_rc, t_rc

Read the camera pose in the robot frame from TF.

The returned transform maps an optical-frame point p_c to the robot frame as p_r = R_rc @ p_c + t_rc. The camera optical axes are right, down, and forward; the robot axes are forward, left, and up.

Args: robot_frame: Target robot frame in which points should be expressed.

camera_frame:
    Source optical frame attached to the depth camera.

Returns: A tuple (R_rc, t_rc) containing a 3 x 3 rotation matrix and a three-element translation vector in meters.

Raises: tf2_ros.LookupException: If no transform is available for the named frames.

tf2_ros.ConnectivityException:
    If the TF tree cannot connect the frames.

tf2_ros.ExtrapolationException:
    If TF cannot satisfy the requested timestamp.

Notes: This method is intended to run once after the robot and camera frames have been published. It waits up to five seconds in the initial availability check.

def deactivate_camera(self): 
449    def deactivate_camera(self):
450        """
451        Unregister camera subscribers and discard their cached data.
452
453        Notes:
454            Clearing the cached frames forces a later activation cycle to wait
455            for fresh camera data instead of reusing an old observation.
456        """
457        for sub in [self.color_sub, self.depth_sub, self.info_sub]:
458            if sub is not None:
459                sub.unregister()
460
461        self.color_sub = None
462        self.depth_sub = None
463        self.info_sub = None
464
465
466        # Clear latest data, so that on the next activation we wait for fresh data
467        self.color_image = None
468        self.depth_image = None
469        self.latest_info = None

def get_forward_displacement_since_start(self): 
713    def get_forward_displacement_since_start(self):
714        """
715        Measure motion along the corridor-definition heading.
716
717        Returns:
718            Signed displacement in meters along the yaw recorded when the
719            current corridor was defined.
720
721        Notes:
722            Projecting world translation onto a fixed heading keeps the result
723            independent of later yaw corrections.
724        """
725
726        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
727        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
728
729        return dx * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)

Measure motion along the corridor-definition heading.

Returns: Signed displacement in meters along the yaw recorded when the current corridor was defined.

Notes: Projecting world translation onto a fixed heading keeps the result independent of later yaw corrections.

def get_lateral_displacement_since_start(self): 
731    def get_lateral_displacement_since_start(self):
732        """
733        Measure motion perpendicular to the corridor-definition heading.
734
735        Returns:
736            Signed lateral displacement in meters in the reference frame that
737            was active when the corridor was defined.
738
739        Notes:
740            The sign follows the left-handed lateral basis produced by
741            ``(-sin(yaw), cos(yaw))``.
742        """
743
744        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
745        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
746
747        return -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)

Measure motion perpendicular to the corridor-definition heading.

Returns: Signed lateral displacement in meters in the reference frame that was active when the corridor was defined.

Notes: The sign follows the left-handed lateral basis produced by (-sin(yaw), cos(yaw)).

def calculate_dynamic_x_corridor_center_in_cameraframe(self): 
749    def calculate_dynamic_x_corridor_center_in_cameraframe(self):
750        """
751        Estimate the apparent lateral corridor shift from odometry.
752
753        Translation perpendicular to the initial heading and the image shift
754        caused by accumulated yaw are added together.
755
756        Returns:
757            Estimated horizontal corridor-center displacement in meters.
758
759        Notes:
760            The rotational term uses the current distance to the corridor
761            midpoint, so the estimate grows as heading error acts over a longer
762            viewing distance.
763        """
764
765        dx = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
766        dy = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
767        
768        #translation effect
769        # Project displacement onto perpendicular to initial heading
770        lateral_displacement = -dx * np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition) + dy * np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)
771
772        #rotation effect
773        # rotation effect
774        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
775        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
776
777        rotation_shift = (self.corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis * np.tan(delta_yaw))
778    
779        
780        rospy.loginfo(f"start pose is {self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition} and current pose is {self.current_pose}   Lateral displacement from start: {lateral_displacement:.3f} m   Rotation shift: {rotation_shift:.3f} m")
781        
782        
783        return (
784        lateral_displacement
785        + rotation_shift
786    )

Estimate the apparent lateral corridor shift from odometry.

Translation perpendicular to the initial heading and the image shift caused by accumulated yaw are added together.

Returns: Estimated horizontal corridor-center displacement in meters.

Notes: The rotational term uses the current distance to the corridor midpoint, so the estimate grows as heading error acts over a longer viewing distance.

def find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(self, final_points_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance): 
790    def find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(self, final_points_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance):
791        """
792        Slide a robot-width window and choose a clear centerline.
793
794        Candidate centers span the camera field of view in corridor
795        coordinates. A candidate is valid when its nearest obstacle is beyond
796        ``min_clearance``. Among valid candidates, the center closest to the
797        robot's current forward axis is preferred.
798
799        Args:
800            final_points_robot_frame:
801                ``N x 2`` array of filtered obstacle points on the robot-frame
802                ground plane, in meters.
803
804            z_max:
805                Far search distance in meters. It defines the visible lateral
806                span and is used as clearance when a candidate contains no
807                obstacle points.
808
809            min_clearance:
810                Minimum acceptable forward clearance in meters.
811
812        Returns:
813            Lateral center coordinate of the best corridor in meters, or
814            ``None`` when no robot-width candidate meets the clearance
815            requirement.
816
817        Notes:
818            Candidate width includes the configured robot half-width and safety
819            margin.
820        """
821        # find best corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
822        # final points are in robot frame
823
824
825        forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
826        lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame = final_points_robot_frame@self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
827
828
829        H, W = self.depth_image.shape
830        x_edge_camera_frame = (W / 2.0) * z_max / self.fx
831
832        left_edge_camera_frame  = np.array([-x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
833        right_edge_camera_frame = np.array([ x_edge_camera_frame, 0.0, z_max])
834
835        left_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ left_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
836        right_edge_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ right_edge_camera_frame + self.t_rc
837
838        left_edge_corridor_frame = left_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
839        right_edge_corridor_frame = right_edge_robot_frame[:2] @ self.corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_first_time_robot_frame
840
841        lat_min_corridor_frame = min(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
842        lat_max_corridor_frame = max(left_edge_corridor_frame, right_edge_corridor_frame)
843        slide_centers_corridor_frame = np.arange(lat_min_corridor_frame + self.half_width, lat_max_corridor_frame - self.half_width, self.slide_step_x_direction)
844        # because lateral min and max depends on entire image,not just on the obstacle points. 
845
846        valid_corridors = []
847
848        for lat_c in slide_centers_corridor_frame:
849            x_left  = lat_c - self.half_width
850            x_right = lat_c + self.half_width
851
852            corridor_mask = (
853                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame > x_left) &
854                (lateral_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame < x_right)
855            )
856
857            corridor_forward_coordinates = forward_coordinate_of_points_in_corridor_frame[corridor_mask]
858
859            # no points in corridor means free of obstacles
860            if len(corridor_forward_coordinates) == 0:
861                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = z_max
862            else:
863                front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor = np.min(corridor_forward_coordinates)
864
865            if front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor >= min_clearance:
866                valid_corridors.append({
867                    "x_center": lat_c,
868                    "clearance": front_clearance_for_virtual_corridor,
869                })
870
871        def corridor_cost(c):
872            """
873            Score one valid corridor by distance from the forward axis.
874
875            Args:
876                c:
877                    Dictionary with ``x_center`` and ``clearance`` entries.
878
879            Returns:
880                Non-negative lateral cost in meters. Smaller is preferred.
881            """
882            lateral_cost   = abs(c["x_center"] - 0.0)  # prefer corridors near center of robot fov (x=0 in camera frame)
883
884            return lateral_cost
885        
886        if len(valid_corridors) == 0:
887            rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid virtual corridor for passability check.")
888            # there is no virtual corridor available. you cannot consider in front of the robot as coridor. because there may be no passable corridor at all
889            return None
890        
891        best_corridor = min(valid_corridors, key=corridor_cost) # it iterates over the list of dicts and passes each dict to corridor_cost
892
893        rospy.loginfo(f"Virtual corridor center defined at x: {best_corridor['x_center']:.3f} m in camera frame")
894        return best_corridor['x_center']

Slide a robot-width window and choose a clear centerline.

Candidate centers span the camera field of view in corridor coordinates. A candidate is valid when its nearest obstacle is beyond min_clearance. Among valid candidates, the center closest to the robot's current forward axis is preferred.

Args: final_points_robot_frame: N x 2 array of filtered obstacle points on the robot-frame ground plane, in meters.

z_max:
    Far search distance in meters. It defines the visible lateral
    span and is used as clearance when a candidate contains no
    obstacle points.

min_clearance:
    Minimum acceptable forward clearance in meters.

Returns: Lateral center coordinate of the best corridor in meters, or None when no robot-width candidate meets the clearance requirement.

Notes: Candidate width includes the configured robot half-width and safety margin.

def find_a_virtual_corridor(self, z_min, z_max, min_clearance): 
897    def find_a_virtual_corridor(self, z_min, z_max, min_clearance):
898        """
899        Search the full depth image for a clear robot-width corridor.
900
901        Depth pixels in the requested range are back-projected, filtered by the
902        normal/outlier/connected-component pipeline, transformed to the robot
903        frame, and passed to the sliding-window corridor search.
904
905        Args:
906            z_min:
907                Nearest depth included in the search, in meters.
908
909            z_max:
910                Farthest depth included in the search, in meters.
911
912            min_clearance:
913                Required obstacle-free distance in meters.
914
915        Returns:
916            A tuple ``(center, image)``. ``center`` is the selected lateral
917            coordinate in the corridor frame, ``0.0`` when filtering finds no
918            obstacles, or ``None`` when obstacles leave no valid candidate.
919            ``image`` is the passability visualization.
920
921        Notes:
922            An empty point cloud is interpreted as open space within the
923            requested depth interval, so the forward axis is selected.
924        """
925        rospy.loginfo("Finding virtual corridor for passability check.")
926       
927
928        # run passability check for full width of image to find a virtual corridor
929
930        valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame, _ = backproject_depth_to_points(
931            self.depth_image, self.fx, self.fy, self.cx, self.cy,
932            max_depth=z_max, min_depth=z_min,
933            subsample=self.subsample, roi_polygon=None
934        )
935        
936        if len(valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) == 0:
937            rospy.logwarn("No valid depth points after back-projection. Cannot define virtual corridor. but it is also possible that there is no points at all because entire region in front is free because of small depth range. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
938            x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
939            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, self.color_image
940        else:
941            corridor_mask_camera_frame = (
942                valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[:, 1] > -self.robot_height_above_camera_level
943            )
944            #we are in camera frame so y down is positive. so we check if points are below the camera height (which means above the ground) by checking if y is greater than -robot_height_above_camera_level. level of camera is 0 in camera frame, and ground is at positive in camera frame. 
945            # no image cropping. we need to check entire image for passability. 
946            corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = valid_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
947            corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame[corridor_mask_camera_frame]
948            
949            _, image, final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame = self.passability_checker.run(
950                self.depth_image,
951                self.color_image,
952                corridor_pts_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
953                corridor_uv_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame,
954                z_max
955            )
956
957            if final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame is not None and len(final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame) > 0:
958                final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = (self.R_rc @ final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_camera_frame.T).T + self.t_rc 
959                # Keep only ground-plane components. Project to ground plane (robot X–Y)
960                final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame = final_points_3d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame[:, :2]  # Extract 2D points (x, y)
961                # donot use the value of front clearance directly because corridor is not defined yet.  this front clerance is for full width of image
962                # we need to find a virtual corridor center based on final points obtained from passability checker
963                
964
965                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = self.find_best_corridor_center_based_on_final_points(final_points_2d_for_virtual_corridor_definition_robot_frame, z_max, min_clearance)
966                #x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame value can be None or a float value. if it is None, it means no valid corridor is found. if it is a float value, it means the x center of the virtual corridor in the corridor frame is at that value. positive value means right side of the robot and negative value means left side of the robot. and 0 means directly in front of the robot.
967            else: # in this case, consider image center as virtual corridor center
968                rospy.logwarn("Cannot find any valid points after filtering for virtual corridor definition. This is possible that there is no points left after filtering, means entire region in front is free. consider virtual corridor is directly in front of robot.")
969                x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame = 0.0
970            
971            return x_virtual_corridor_center_corridor_frame, image

Search the full depth image for a clear robot-width corridor.

Depth pixels in the requested range are back-projected, filtered by the normal/outlier/connected-component pipeline, transformed to the robot frame, and passed to the sliding-window corridor search.

Args: z_min: Nearest depth included in the search, in meters.

z_max:
    Farthest depth included in the search, in meters.

min_clearance:
    Required obstacle-free distance in meters.

Returns: A tuple (center, image). center is the selected lateral coordinate in the corridor frame, 0.0 when filtering finds no obstacles, or None when obstacles leave no valid candidate. image is the passability visualization.

Notes: An empty point cloud is interpreted as open space within the requested depth interval, so the forward axis is selected.

def relative_robot_motion(self): 
 973    def relative_robot_motion(self):
 974        """
 975        Compute robot motion since the current corridor was defined.
 976
 977        Returns:
 978            A tuple ``(R, t)``. ``R`` is the planar rotation from the corridor
 979            definition orientation to the current orientation, and ``t`` is
 980            current translation expressed in the definition frame.
 981
 982        Notes:
 983            Yaw difference is wrapped to ``[-pi, pi]`` before constructing the
 984            rotation matrix.
 985        """
 986
 987        dx_world = self.current_pose[0] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[0]
 988        dy_world = self.current_pose[1] - self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition[1]
 989        delta_yaw = self.current_yaw - self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition
 990        delta_yaw = np.arctan2(np.sin(delta_yaw), np.cos(delta_yaw))
 991
 992        # Rotation matrix (start -> current)
 993        R = np.array([
 994            [ np.cos(delta_yaw), -np.sin(delta_yaw)],
 995            [ np.sin(delta_yaw),  np.cos(delta_yaw)]
 996        ])
 997
 998        R_world_to_R0 = np.array([
 999            [ np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)],
1000            [-np.sin(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition),  np.cos(self.start_yaw_at_corridor_definition)]
1001        ])
1002
1003        t = R_world_to_R0 @ np.array([dx_world, dy_world])
1004        return R, t

Compute robot motion since the current corridor was defined.

Returns: A tuple (R, t). R is the planar rotation from the corridor definition orientation to the current orientation, and t is current translation expressed in the definition frame.

Notes: Yaw difference is wrapped to [-pi, pi] before constructing the rotation matrix.

def propagate_corridor_point(self, corridor_point_R0, R, t): 
1006    def propagate_corridor_point(self, corridor_point_R0,R, t):
1007        """
1008        Propagate a fixed corridor point into the current robot frame.
1009
1010        Args:
1011            corridor_point_R0:
1012                Two-element corridor point expressed in the robot frame at
1013                corridor-definition time.
1014
1015            R:
1016                Current planar rotation relative to the definition frame, as
1017                returned by :meth:`relative_robot_motion`.
1018
1019            t:
1020                Current planar translation in the definition frame.
1021
1022        Returns:
1023            Two-element ``[forward, lateral]`` point in the current robot
1024            frame.
1025        """
1026
1027        # Extract x,z (planar)
1028        p0 = np.array([
1029            corridor_point_R0[0],
1030            corridor_point_R0[1]
1031        ])
1032
1033        # Inverse robot motion
1034        p_now = R.T @ (p0 - t)
1035
1036        return p_now  # [X_forward, Y_lateral] in robot frame

Propagate a fixed corridor point into the current robot frame.

Args: corridor_point_R0: Two-element corridor point expressed in the robot frame at corridor-definition time.

R:
    Current planar rotation relative to the definition frame, as
    returned by `relative_robot_motion()`.

t:
    Current planar translation in the definition frame.

Returns: Two-element [forward, lateral] point in the current robot frame.

def project_to_pixel(self, P_cam): 
1038    def project_to_pixel(self, P_cam):
1039        """
1040        Project one camera-frame point into image coordinates.
1041
1042        Args:
1043            P_cam:
1044                Three-element ``(X, Y, Z)`` camera-frame point in meters.
1045
1046        Returns:
1047            Integer ``(u, v)`` pixel coordinates, or ``None`` when the point is
1048            on or behind the camera plane.
1049        """
1050        X, Y, Z = P_cam
1051        if Z <= 0:
1052            return None
1053        u = int(self.fx * X / Z + self.cx)
1054        v = int(self.fy * Y / Z + self.cy)
1055        return (u, v)

Project one camera-frame point into image coordinates.

Args: P_cam: Three-element (X, Y, Z) camera-frame point in meters.

Returns: Integer (u, v) pixel coordinates, or None when the point is on or behind the camera plane.

def run(self): 
1058    def run(self):
1059        """
1060        Define, propagate, and evaluate corridors until ROS shuts down.
1061
1062        On activation, the loop first defines a corridor from detected door
1063        geometry. A later traversal request can replace it with a virtual
1064        corridor selected from the visible free space. Each iteration uses
1065        odometry to express the fixed corridor in the current robot frame,
1066        chooses either corridor or local passability mode, filters the
1067        relevant RGB-D points, and publishes clearance and alignment data.
1068
1069        The traversal trigger is latched after the original corridor first
1070        provides enough clearance through and beyond the door. Optional
1071        visualization projects the evaluated corridor boundaries back into the
1072        color image.
1073
1074        Raises:
1075            cv_bridge.CvBridgeError:
1076                If a generated visualization cannot be converted to a ROS
1077                image outside the guarded visualization-publish block.
1078
1079        Notes:
1080            This is a blocking node loop. Subscriber callbacks only cache
1081            state; all expensive point-cloud work is performed here at the
1082            configured five-hertz rate.
1083        """
1084        while not rospy.is_shutdown():
1085            if not self.active: # node inactive, skip processing. node will be activated when door state is open_left or open_right and 
1086                #de activated when traversal done signal is received
1087                self.rate.sleep()
1088                continue
1089            
1090            # this is to wait until first time data is ready after activation
1091            if not self.first_time_data_ready_after_node_activation(): # if data not ready, wait
1092                self.rate.sleep()
1093                continue
1094
1095            
1096            # because ros subscriber callbacks and main loop are in different threads, it is possible that during main loop execution 
1097            # new data could come in self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node. but it is okay because the new data will be used in next iteration of main loop.
1098            # but we cannot use self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node directly here because it may change during execution of this main loop iteration.

1101                # consider the value from call back if traversal node is triggered. its fine that, setting trigger_traversal_node to true doesnt mean value will be available at 
1102                # first iteration itself. because in that case we can wait for next iteration to get the value. because subscriber cb will only be called when new data arrives.
1103                # so this if check block avoid setting type_of_passability_check to default 0 when trigger_traversal_node is true and requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node is not yet set by callback.
1104                type_of_passability_check = self.requested_type_of_passability_check_from_traversal_node

1106

1112                self.start_pose_at_corridor_definition = self.current_pose  # store the pose at corridor definition time
1113                clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor = self.min_corridor_clearance_beyond_door_to_trigger_traversal_node #value is considering robot should pass through the door. this info is not from traversal node but from the parameter server because it is related to the door and corridor, not related to the robot pose which is updated in real time. so it should be a fixed value instead of dynamic value updated from traversal node

1117

1119                plane_info_norm_robot_frame = self.R_rc @ self.plane_info_norm_camera_frame

1482                        # So:Forward axis = robot X,  Lateral axis = robot Y, Up axis = robot Z . No rotated basis needed.
1483                        # Near boundary (z_min)
1484                        left_line_start_robot_frame  = np.array([z_min,  self.half_width, 0.0])
1485                        right_line_start_robot_frame = np.array([z_min, -self.half_width, 0.0])
1486
1487                        # Far boundary (z_max)
1488                        left_line_end_robot_frame   = np.array([z_max,  self.half_width, 0.0])
1489                        right_line_end_robot_frame  = np.array([z_max, -self.half_width, 0.0])
1490                        #Transform to Camera Frame
1491                        left_line_start_camera_frame  = self.R_rc.T @ (left_line_start_robot_frame - self.t_rc)
1492                        right_line_start_camera_frame = self.R_rc.T @ (right_line_start_robot_frame - self.t_rc)
1493                        left_line_end_camera_frame    = self.R_rc.T @ (left_line_end_robot_frame - self.t_rc)
1494                        right_line_end_camera_frame   = self.R_rc.T @ (right_line_end_robot_frame - self.t_rc)
1495
1496
1497                valid_points_3d_camera_frame, uv, _ = backproject_depth_to_points(
1498                    self.depth_image, self.fx, self.fy, self.cx, self.cy,
1499                    max_depth=z_max, min_depth=z_min,
1500                    subsample=self.subsample, roi_polygon=None
1501                )
1502
1503                rospy.loginfo(f"minimum depth is {self.depth_image.min()} and maximum depth is {self.depth_image.max()} for the current depth image used in passability check.")
1504                rospy.loginfo(f"z_min is {z_min} and z_max is {z_max} for back projection in passability check. number of valid depth points for passability check is {len(valid_points_3d_camera_frame)}")
1505                if len(valid_points_3d_camera_frame) == 0: 
1506                    rospy.logwarn("No valid depth points for passability check.")
1507                    front_clearance = z_max
1508                    passability_view = self.color_image
1509
1510                else:
1511                    valid_points_3d_robot_frame = (self.R_rc @ valid_points_3d_camera_frame.T).T + self.t_rc 
1512                    # Keep only ground-plane components
1513                    valid_points_2d_robot_frame = valid_points_3d_robot_frame[:, :2]  # Extract 2D points (x, y)
1514                    
1515                    if type_of_passability_check == 1: # corridor passability check, we need to consider the points within the corridor defined by the corridor axis and robot width. so we need to calculate the lateral and forward distance of the points with respect to the corridor axis and keep only the points within the corridor.
1516                        # -------------------------------------------------
1517                        # Express relative to corridor center
1518                        # -------------------------------------------------
1519
1520                        delta = valid_points_2d_robot_frame - Pr_now   # (N,2)
1521                        # -------------------------------------------------
1522                        # Project onto corridor axes
1523                        # -------------------------------------------------
1524
1525                        lateral_values = delta @ corridor_lateral_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now
1526                        forward_values = delta @ corridor_forward_2d_unit_vector_robot_frame_now
1527                    
1528                    elif type_of_passability_check == 2: # local passability check, we need to consider the points within the area in front of the robot defined by the robot width and the z_max for local passability check. so we need to calculate the lateral and forward distance of the points with respect to the robot frame and keep only the points within the area in front of the robot.
1529                        # for local passability, we use robot forward axis as reference, so we can directly use the x and y values in robot frame to calculate the lateral and forward distance of the points with respect to the robot frame. and we do not need to express the points relative to corridor center because local passability is purely robot-centric and does not depend on corridor definition. so we can directly calculate the lateral and forward distance of the points with respect to the robot frame without considering the corridor center.
1530                        lateral_values = valid_points_2d_robot_frame[:, 1]  # y values in robot frame represent lateral distance (left is positive, right is negative)
1531                        forward_values = valid_points_2d_robot_frame[:, 0]  # x values
1532              
1533                    camera_height_in_robot_base = self.t_rc[2]  # z component of camera translation in robot base frame represents the camera height from the ground
1534                    mask_below_robot_eye_level = (
1535                            valid_points_3d_robot_frame[:, 2] < camera_height_in_robot_base + self.robot_height_above_camera_level
1536                        )
1537                    
1538                    corridor_mask_robot_frame = (
1539                        (np.abs(lateral_values) < self.half_width) &
1540                        (forward_values >= 0) &  # only consider points in front of the robot
1541                        (forward_values <= z_max) & # only consider points within the max depth for passability check
1542                        mask_below_robot_eye_level #
1543                    )
1544
1545                    corridor_pts_camera_frame = valid_points_3d_camera_frame[corridor_mask_robot_frame]
1546                    corridor_uv_camera_frame = uv[corridor_mask_robot_frame]
1547                    
1548                    # not using final points here as the corridor is already defined
1549                    front_clearance, passability_view, _ = self.passability_checker.run(
1550                        self.depth_image,
1551                        self.color_image,
1552                        corridor_pts_camera_frame,
1553                        corridor_uv_camera_frame,
1554                        z_max
1555                    )
1556
1557            #to trigger the traversal node based on corridor passability result
1558            if self.trigger_traversal_node is False and type_of_passability_check == 1 and front_clearance is not None: # if traversal node is not yet triggered, we can do passability check and trigger traversal node based on the result. but once traversal node is triggered, we should not reset the trigger even if passability goes false in later iterations. because it only makes sense to trigger traversal node once when we detect passability for the first time. and during traversal passability may go false but we do not want to retrigger traversal node.
1559                #executes only once
1560                corridor_Passability_status = front_clearance > self.corridor_middle_point_depth_dynamic_along_corridor_axis + self.min_corridor_clearance_beyond_door_to_trigger_traversal_node
1561                if corridor_Passability_status:
1562                    # trigger traversal node if it is passable for the first time.
1563                    #but in later if instantanous passability goes false, do not reset the trigger
1564                    #trigger traverse node once we detect passability. but during the traversal passability
1565                    # may be false, we do not want to retrigger the traversal node.
1566                    self.trigger_traversal_node = True
1567
1568                #in local passability check we do not trigger traversal node, because it is already triggered in corridor passability check which will execute first
1569
1570                             
1571
1572            get_duration_seconds.write_text_file()
1573
1574
1575            self.trigger_traversal_node_pub.publish(Bool(data=self.trigger_traversal_node))
1576
1577            msg = Robot_passability()
1578            msg.front_clearance = float(front_clearance) if front_clearance is not None else float('nan')
1579            msg.x_corridor_center_start_yaw_frame = float(x_corridor_center_start_yaw_frame) if x_corridor_center_start_yaw_frame is not None else float('nan')
1580            msg.type_of_passability_check = type_of_passability_check # 1 for corridor , 2 for local
1581            msg.x_corridor_center_cam = float(x_corridor_center_cam) if x_corridor_center_cam is not None else float('nan')
1582            msg.corridor_middle_point_depth = float(corridor_middle_point_depth) if corridor_middle_point_depth is not None else float('nan')
1583            msg.clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor = float(clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor) if clearance_needed_beyond_mid_corridor is not None else float('nan')
1584            msg.heading_error = float(heading_error) if heading_error is not None else float('nan')
1585
1586            #publish results
1587            self.Passability_pub.publish(msg)
1588
1589            # Publish visualizations
1590            try:
1591                if self.enable_visualization and passability_view is not None:
1592                    # Convert boundaries to pixel coordinates for visualization    
1593                    #x_left_boundary_uv = int((x_left_limit * self.fx) / reference_depth_for_visualization + self.cx)
1594                    #x_right_boundary_uv = int((x_right_limit * self.fx) / reference_depth_for_visualization + self.cx)
1595                    #cv2.line(passability_view, (x_left_boundary_uv, 0), (x_left_boundary_uv, passability_view.shape[0]), (0, 165, 255), 4)  # orange
1596                    #cv2.line(passability_view, (x_right_boundary_uv, 0), (x_right_boundary_uv, passability_view.shape[0]), (0, 0, 255), 4)  # red
1597                    p1 = self.project_to_pixel(left_line_start_camera_frame)
1598                    p2 = self.project_to_pixel(left_line_end_camera_frame)
1599                    p3 = self.project_to_pixel(right_line_start_camera_frame)
1600                    p4 = self.project_to_pixel(right_line_end_camera_frame)
1601
1602                    # Draw lines on the passability view
1603                    cv2.line(passability_view, p1, p2, (0, 255, 0), 2)  # green
1604                    cv2.line(passability_view, p3, p4, (0, 0, 255), 2)  # red
1605                    
1606                    self.passability_view_pub.publish(self.bridge.cv2_to_imgmsg(passability_view, encoding="bgr8"))
1607
1608            except Exception as e:
1609                rospy.logdebug(f"Viz publish exception: {e}")
1610
1611
1612            self.rate.sleep()

Define, propagate, and evaluate corridors until ROS shuts down.

On activation, the loop first defines a corridor from detected door geometry. A later traversal request can replace it with a virtual corridor selected from the visible free space. Each iteration uses odometry to express the fixed corridor in the current robot frame, chooses either corridor or local passability mode, filters the relevant RGB-D points, and publishes clearance and alignment data.

The traversal trigger is latched after the original corridor first provides enough clearance through and beyond the door. Optional visualization projects the evaluated corridor boundaries back into the color image.

Raises: cv_bridge.CvBridgeError: If a generated visualization cannot be converted to a ROS image outside the guarded visualization-publish block.

Notes: This is a blocking node loop. Subscriber callbacks only cache state; all expensive point-cloud work is performed here at the configured five-hertz rate.
